messages:
Sophie T.: heads up — escalation from account acct-ACME, case #45231. They see lots of short bursts (dozens of parallel small requests) and then intermittent 429s + long tail latency (700–1500ms) for completions. They insist they are under monthly quota but we see perceived throttling when bursts happen. Repro info below, copying logs they attached.

Raj P.: can you paste a sample request id and model? also did they pin a model variant or use streaming? common culprits: per-route qps limits, continous batching backpressure, and cold KV cache churn.

Sophie T.: sample request id from their logs: req=01G7X3JQ9A1, model=redwood-v2-large, route=/v1/chat/completions. They use non-streaming, many 1–5 token prompts (prompt templates + metadata) coming from web clients in spikes. They said headers show 200 until it 'suddenly' starts spiking 429.

Mike L.: quick note — small token requests are the worst for perceived throttling because continuous batching tries to merge them and then you get head-of-line/backpressure. if backend is at capacity, batching window will delay until batch fills, which increases latency and can cause upstream queues to saturate, leading to rate limiting on our side. also KV cache cold-misses for many slightly different prefixes can blow up compute.

Support Bot: Case 45231 linked to this thread. Assigned to eng-oncall.

Raj P.: to debug we need: exact timestamps (start/end), request ids (a few around a spike), client concurrency, and if they have any per-api-key quotas set. Also ask them to provide the raw request payload (strip secrets). Meanwhile, we can pull proxy logs for the timeframe.

Sophie T.: provided logs for 14:22–14:30 UTC, attaching few lines they sent:
```
[2026-03-12T14:22:10Z] req=01G7X3JQ9A1 status=200 model=redwood-v2-large latency_ms=210 tokens_out=12 client=web-frontend
[2026-03-12T14:22:12Z] req=01G7X3JQF2 status=429 reason=burst_quota_exceeded route=/v1/chat/completions client=web-frontend
[2026-03-12T14:22:12Z] req=01G7X3JR3 status=429 reason=quota_exhausted route=/v1/chat/completions
[2026-03-12T14:22:13Z] req=01G7X3JS4 status=200 model=redwood-v2-large latency_ms=980 tokens_out=5
```

Mike L.: the presence of both 200 and 429 at the same second is classic burst-handling — our rate limiter tries to let some requests through and rejects others when concurrency or short-term burst budget is spent. note the high 980ms latency on one 200 — likely a large batching window or KV miss.

Emma R.: quick repro script we asked them to run:
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat/completions" \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"redwood-v2-large","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":8}' &
  sleep 0.01
done
wait
```
Asking them to run with and without `sleep` to see burst behavior. Also asked to run with `stream=true` to compare.

Raj P.: while they run that, I'll pull infra metrics: per-key qps, per-route qps, batching window size distribution, KV cache hit rate, and avg batch size. I suspect batch size is small (1–3) and batching window is set to 20ms which combined with high request rate causes many batches and queuing.

Incident Bot: Alert: high 429 rate detected for api_key acct-ACME between 2026-03-12T14:21:50Z and 14:25:00Z — spike of 140 429s/min.

Sophie T.: customer confirms they do 200 concurrent short prompts for certain flows — they can change client behavior but want us to confirm server-side options first. They say they cannot stream because of client constraints.

Mike L.: mitigation options (in order):
- short-term: grant a temporary burst allowance for the account (increase leaky-bucket limit for 60s) so they don't hit 429s mid-session.
- mid-term: encourage client-side batching (combine multiple short prompts per request) or introduce a cheap prefix consolidation / semantic dedupe.
- infra: increase per-route concurrency and tune continuous batching parameters (reduce max wait, raise max_batch_size threshold).
- KV cache: warm frequently used prefixes via a background warmup job or prefetch when user session starts.

Raj P.: pulled metrics — avg_batch_size=2.1 (bad), kv_cache_hit=12% during spike (very bad), per-key short_term_burst_budget depleted repeatedly. I created a short dashboard and attached a permalink.

Sophie T.: customer asked for exact steps we will take. I'll propose: temporary +2x burst budget for next 48h, guidance doc for client changes, and an eng task to tune batching/KV warmup if we see recurrence. they agreed to run the curl test.

Emma R.: sample client change examples: combine prompts into one messages array when possible, or buffer 50–100ms on the client to let batching coalesce at the gateway side instead of many tiny requests. example pseudo: 
```js
// naive coalescing queue
const q = [];
function sendPrompt(p) { q.push(p); }
setInterval(async ()=>{ if(q.length){ await api.chat.completions({messages:[...q.splice(0,20)], max_tokens:32}) } }, 50)
```
This reduces number of HTTP connections and KV churn.

Raj P.: also check that client isn't setting different prompt prefixes every time (like session_id or timestamp) which invalidates KV caching. suggest extracting stable prefix and sending variable parts in metadata so KV cache can reuse.

Mike L.: action taken: applied temporary per-key burst allowance +200 for 1 hour for acct-ACME and increased per-route short-window QPS by 50% for the same window. I'll monitor.

Sophie T.: customer ran the script — they report 429s dropped from ~35% to ~3% in subsequent run. Latencies improved (p95 from 1.1s to 420ms). They are happy with temporary fix.

Raj P.: next tasks: create permanent runbook entry about "small-request burst patterns" and recommended customer-side mitigations, add a KV-warmup playground doc for SEs, and schedule eng task to tune continuous batching defaults (investigate dynamic windows based on incoming QPS).

Emma R.: quick note for docs: include sample header check for clients to surface X-RateLimit-Remaining and Retry-After and log them in client telemetry so customers can self-diagnose.

Support Bot: Case 45231 status updated -> temporary-burst-granted.

Mike L.: monitoring update — after changes, 429 spike subsided. kv_cache_hit improved to ~48% after customer applied prefix consolidation. Closing on our side unless they reopen.

Sophie T.: marking as resolved with follow-ups: (1) send customer how-to for prefix consolidation + coalescing; (2) include the runbook link; (3) eng task ID INF-3124 for batching tuning.

Emma R.: adding final snippets they can share with devs:
- check for variable prefixes
- batch on client where feasible
- respect Retry-After and implement exponential backoff
- use streaming if latency-sensitive

Sophie T.: resolved — closing thread. :white_check_mark:
